name: Fetch (reference server)
outcome_statement: As of 2026-11-14: meets C1, C2, C3, C4, C5, C6, C10; partly meets C7, C8, C9.

findings.title: Source and release provenance
findings.finding: The PyPI record for mcp-server-fetch 2026.11.11 links the repository, and PyPI holds a provenance attestation for the release naming `modelcontextprotocol/servers` (workflow `release.yml`) as publisher.

findings.title: Published security policy
findings.finding: GitHub shows a security policy for the repository (`SECURITY.md` in the repository), and it describes how to report a vulnerability.

findings.title: Maintenance status
findings.finding: The repository is not archived and the package is not marked deprecated. Latest release 2026.11.11 is dated 2026-11-11; the newest commit on `main` is dated 2026-11-11; GitHub reports the last push on 2026-11-12.

findings.title: Published advisories
findings.finding: 5 advisories are published in the repository's advisory list for mcp-server-fetch; each names a patched version at or below the latest release (2026.11.11). Most recent: GHSA-3rxj-6jhw-qfv7 (low, published 2026-11-11, patched in 2026.11.11).

findings.title: Documented scope controls
findings.finding: The single tool is documented as read-only. Quoted: “Annotations: `readOnlyHint: true`, `destructiveHint: false`, `idempotentHint: true`, `openWorldHint: true` (it only reads, and it reaches arbitrary hosts on the internet)”.

findings.title: Credential handling in the documented setup
findings.finding: The documented setup takes no credential. Searched `src/fetch/README.md` for: API_KEY, _TOKEN\b, password.

findings.title: Telemetry and outbound data, as documented
findings.finding: The documented function is retrieving arbitrary web addresses; the README documents a private-address guard and an optional host allowlist. It contains no reference to telemetry. Searched `src/fetch/README.md` for: telemetry, usage statistics, usage stats, we collect, data collection, opt-out, posthog. Quoted: “By default the server may fetch from any host (subject to the private-address guard above).”.

findings.title: Dependency management files
findings.finding: A lockfile (`package-lock.json`) is committed. No Dependabot or Renovate configuration file exists at the paths listed in the methodology.

findings.title: Documentation of untrusted-content risk
findings.finding: The README carries a caution about what the server can reach; it does not name prompt injection or untrusted content. Quoted: “This server can access local/internal IP addresses and may represent a security risk. Exercise caution when using this MCP server to ensure this does not expose any sensitive data.”.

findings.title: Currency of the declared MCP library
findings.finding: Declared MCP library: mcp<3,>=2.3. Lower-bound version 2.3.0 of mcp (PyPI) was published on 2026-10-02, within the 12 months before 2026-11-14.

advisories.summary: mcp-server-fetch: IPv6 site-local fec0::/10 classified as public (SSRF guard classifier gap, CWE-918)
mcp-server-fetch: robots.txt path-canonicalization bypass (e.g. //private fetched while Disallow: /private)
robots.txt enforcement bypass via HTTP redirects in mcp-server-fetch
fetch server: SSRF guard treats the well-known NAT64 prefix 64:ff9b::/96 as public, so a metadata address is reachable on NAT64/DNS64 egress
fetch: private-address guard bypass via IDNA hostnames (check and connect resolve different names)
